look: Grand stone palaces and long classical fronts painted yellow, green, pink and white, along wide straight avenues and canals. Gold spires and domes rose over the skyline.
Men in long coats with peaked caps or fur hats, and many in uniform. Coachmen wore thick padded coats. Women wore long skirts and fitted jackets.
Horse cabs, sledges in winter, and horse trams with seats on the roof. Electric trams came only in 1907.
Gas and electric lamps on the main streets. In June the sky hardly gets dark at all: the White Nights.
St Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire. Nicholas II was crowned tsar in May 1896.

stops.name: Nevsky Prospekt, the main street
stops.title: Nevsky Prospekt and the Admiralty
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: A gold spire 72 metres high closes the end of Nevsky Prospekt.
spots.how: It still shines at the end of the street today.

spots.d: Shop names in Russian and German. Many merchants in the capital came from German families.
spots.how: The signs in the photograph are in both alphabets.

spots.d: Rails in the road for horse trams.
Horses pulled every cart and cab in the city.
spots.how: There were no cars here yet.

stops.name: Znamenskaya Square, by the station
stops.title: Znamenskaya Square
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: The church that gave the square its name. It was pulled down in 1940 to build a metro station.
spots.how: Old photographs like this are how we know what it looked like.

spots.d: Passengers could climb up curved stairs and ride on the roof.
spots.how: Horse trams ran here until electric ones came in 1907.

spots.d: Cabs waited for travellers from the Moscow railway station on this square.
spots.how: The station still stands on the square.

spots.d: Most men wear peaked caps and long coats, even in summer.
spots.how: Count the caps in the crowd.

stops.name: Palace Square
stops.title: Palace Square and the Alexander Column
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: 47.5 metres of red granite, set up in 1834 for the victory over Napoleon. It stands by its own weight, with no fixings.
spots.how: It is still there, topped by an angel.

spots.d: A coachman in a padded coat drives a carriage across the square.
spots.how: Photographs of the time show the same thick coats.

spots.d: Palace Square is huge and mostly empty, made for military parades in front of the tsar's Winter Palace.
spots.how: The Winter Palace stands on the square, out of view here.

stops.name: Kazan Cathedral
stops.title: Kazan Cathedral
stops.note: A photochrom: a black-and-white photograph turned into colour by hand-made printing plates, so the colours are close but not exact.

spots.d: Built from 1801 to 1811, with a curved row of 96 columns inspired by St Peter's in Rome.
spots.how: It still stands on Nevsky Prospekt.

spots.d: Low posts and chains kept carriages off the square in front of the cathedral.
spots.how: You can see them running along the front.

spots.d: Nevsky Prospekt got electric street lights in the 1880s.
spots.how: The lamp stands on the avenue in front of the cathedral.
